text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
CanBlock(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Jump(x) ::: x can jump when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Man(x) ::: x is a man.
Michael ::: Michael.
Windy ::: Windy.
Peter ::: Peter.
Class(y, x) ::: y is in the class of x.

Premises:
∀x ∀y (Man(x) ∧ Man(y) ∧ Taller(x, y) → CanBlock(x, y)) ::: If a man is taller than another, he can block his shooting.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z)) → Taller(x, z)) ::: Transitivity of taller relation.
Taller(Michael, y) ∀y (∀z (Taller(y, z) → Taller(Michael, z))) ::: Michael is taller than everyone else in his class.
Taller(Peter, Michael) ::: Peter is taller than Michael.
∀x ∀y (Taller(x, y) ∧ Jump(x) → GreatShooter(x)) ::: Shooters who can jump are great shooters.
¬CanBlock(Michael, Windy) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.

Conclusion:
∃x (Man(x) ∧ Taller(x, Peter)) ::: There exists a man in Michael's class taller than Peter.
